PullRequest.Title: Add hover tooltip for Customizations button in agents sidebar
PullRequest.Body: This pull request implements a hoverable tooltip for the Customizations button in the agents window left sidebar. The tooltip provides users with important information regarding customizations that need to be updated. ### Changes made: - Added a tooltip that displays **“Some customizations need an update to keep working.”** when the yellow migration indicator is present. - The tooltip is implemented using `IHoverService`, supports keyboard focus, and updates reactively based on the migration state. - The tooltip is now anchored to the right edge of the Customizations sidebar button. - Added unit tests to cover both normal and warning tooltip states. ### Validation: - Focused unit tests passed. - ESLint checks completed successfully. - Client type-check and full compilation were successful. - The tooltip behavior has been verified in the running Agents Window.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or rerender the Agents sidebar navigation containing the Customizations row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tree renderer synchronously registers one mouseover listener and one HoverService map entry for the rendered Customizations row; no hover widget is created and no external operation must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales with rendered Customizations rows, whose effective cardinality is one in each applicable navigation/list surface rather than with session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread render; one registration per currently rendered Customizations row. Tree template reuse first clears elementDisposables, and disposal removes the map entry and listener.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lookup or miss behavior is involved. The hover options are deferred until interaction; recycled templates dispose the prior registration before installing another.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderSection, disposeElement/disposeShortcut, DisposableStore cleanup, and HoverService._setupDelayedHover were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact render frequency depends on tree updates and layout, but each render performs only bounded listener/map bookkeeping and does not accumulate registrations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded setup work for a single row, with explicit lifecycle cleanup and no expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pointer hover over the Customizations row with or without a pending migration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On mouseover, HoverService resolves the local observable value and localized string, then lazily creates and displays one hover widget after the configured delay. This is the intended interaction path and has no remote or storage dependency.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per user hover interaction; content selection does not depend on customization count or session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: HoverService maintains one current delayed hover and returns the existing hover when identity matches, so descendant mouseover events do not create a concurrent widget burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No data cache is used. Migration state is already resident in an observable, and hover options are resolved at interaction time rather than cached or eagerly computed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed callback and HoverService showDelayedHover/_createHover flow were inspected, including same-identity coalescing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM/widget construction cost is not measured, but it occurs only after deliberate hover and is bounded to one widget.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly introduced work is lazy, bounded, coalesced, and necessary to provide the hover.

Scenarios.Scenario: Migration availability changes while the Agents sidebar remains open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The state change itself does not execute the added callback; the current value is read only when hover options are requested, so no new work is placed on the migration update path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Independent of update frequency because the added code does not subscribe or autorun on this observable.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No scheduled or concurrent work is introduced by the changed code on state updates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The callback reads the latest in-memory observable value on demand; there is no stale cache, invalidation, negative cache, or miss amplification relevant to performance.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff uses get() inside the delayed hover callback rather than a reactive subscription.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance; the call path is directly visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Migration changes do not trigger repeated rendering or boundary work through the added path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all changed files and diff pages. Traced sidebar rendering, template lifecycle, delayed-hover interaction, migration-state reads, coalescing, and external boundaries. The change adds only constant, lazy hover work with cleanup; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
